Angiofibromas ( Figure 1 ) are benign fibroblastic tumors that histologically comprise bland spindle cells in a variably myxoid to collagenous stroma with a prominent vascular network. They present as telangiectatic, skin colored to pink to red-brown, dome-shaped papules with a glistening surface that primarily occur in the central part of the face, especially the nose. They may be mistaken for acne but do not spontaneously resolve. Facial angiofibromas may also resemble a wide variety of other skin disorders, including rosacea, multiple trichoepitheliomas, eruptive generalized keratoacanthoma

Collagenomas ( Figures 2 , 3 ) are benign connective tissue nevi, which are hamartomas of the dermis, that have a dominant collagen component (36). Histologically, these lesions appear as unencapsulated areas of dense, thick collagen bundles arranged in a haphazard array within the reticular dermis below a region of normal-appearing papillary dermis (13, 37). They present as well-circumscribed, raised (and sometimes pedunculated), round to oval dome-shaped papules that are hypopigmented or skin-colored. tiple reports to have LOH at the MEN1 locus (8, 27, 59–62), consistent with a causal relationship with MEN1, and there are no clear genotype-phenotype correlations (24, 25). Lipomas in MEN1 patients ( Figure 3 ) are not infrequently multiple and are typically subcutaneous, but they can also be found more deeply and reach large sizes that may require surgical extirpation (21, 63–66). Lipomas can also be the first clinical manifestation in MEN1 patients, diagnosed as young as 9 years (24, 67), but there is not a clear correlation with patient age or disease duration (15). B: Cytokeratin immunohistochemistry of the same thymic neuroendocrine tumor in an MEN1 patient; epithelial immunopositivity supports the neuroendocrine carcinoma, consistent with the MEN1 neuroendocrine-tumor histology finding. C: Synaptophysin immunohistochemistry of the thymic neuroendocrine tumor in an MEN1 patient; diffuse neuroendocrine marker positivity confirms the neuroendocrine histology finding. D: Chromogranin A immunohistochemistry of the thymic neuroendocrine tumor in an MEN1 patient; neuroendocrine marker positivity supports the neuroendocrine-tumor histology finding. panels.rationale: Clinical photograph (two seamless views: wide view of the abdominal wall and close-up of a single lesion) showing multiple skin-colored, dome-shaped, smooth-surfaced papules on the periumbilical/anterior abdominal skin. The caption ('Multiple cutaneous collagenomas') and in-text description explicitly identify these as collagenomas in a patient with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 syndrome, and multiple cutaneous collagenomas are a recognized classic cutaneous manifestation of MEN1. panels.figure_caption: Axial views of 68Ga-DOTATOC PET/CT exhibiting neuroendocrine tumors on the head of the pancreas (A, white circle), body (B, white circle), and tail (C, white circle).
in_text_mentions: OTA-D-Phe1-Try3-Octreotide positron emission tomography/computed tomography (68Ga-DOTATOC PET/CT) demonstrated increased somatostatin receptor expression in 3 pancreatic tumors: a 47- × 47-mm nodule in the tail (maximum standardized uptake value, SUVmax 26.2), a 16- × 13-mm in the head (SUVmax 37.9), and an irregular mass in the body (SUVmax 10) (Fig. 1). The patient was asymptomatic, with no clinical evidence of hormone hypersecretion or mass effect. Chromogranin A was within normal limits at 17 µg/L (international system of unit, SI: 38.5 nmol/L) (reference value <100 µg/L; SI: <226 nmol/L).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). Gross pathology revealed a firm, white-yellow, indurated mass in the pancreatic head measuring 3.7 × 3.5 × 3 cm with irregular borders and central hardness (Fig. 4). panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: EUS image from a human MEN1 patient with Zollinger-Ellison syndrome showing diffusely thickened (hypertrophic) gastric rugae, a recognized manifestation of hypergastrinemia in MEN1-associated ZES; caption and in-text confirm diffuse thickening of gastric rugae (echo-layers I-III) in this case, and the article title ties the presentation to MEN1. Finding not in vocabulary, so recorded as proposed. b: EUS image showing a cystic lesion in the pancreatic neck with thick hypoechoic walls, captioned as neuroendocrine tumor and confirmed on FNA as well-differentiated NET, in a human patient with MEN1 (article title: Zollinger Ellison Syndrome in a Patient with Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 1). Pancreatic NET is a hallmark MEN1 manifestation matching the vocabulary finding key.

plate_findings.evidence: symmetrical pituitary gland enlargement with convex superior margin (dotted arrow in A)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Coronal T1 sellar MRI in a patient with MEN1 showing symmetrical pituitary gland enlargement with a convex superior margin, a pituitary manifestation of MEN1. The finding maps to the MEN1 pituitary-lesion vocabulary entry, although the case was ultimately diagnosed as somatotroph hyperplasia rather than a true adenoma. B: Coronal post-contrast T1 sellar MRI in a patient with MEN1 showing a central sellar nodule that was initially interpreted as a pituitary adenoma; part of the MEN1 pituitary manifestation ultimately confirmed as somatotroph hyperplasia. C: Coronal T2 sellar MRI in a patient with MEN1 showing marked T2 hypointensity and a central nodule, features reviewed as pituitary hyperplasia; maps to the MEN1 pituitary-lesion vocabulary entry. D: Sagittal post-contrast T1 sellar MRI in a patient with MEN1 showing pituitary gland enlargement, part of the same MEN1 pituitary manifestation; maps to the MEN1 pituitary-lesion...

panels.figure_caption: Sellar magnetic resonance imaging on A, coronal T1; B, coronal T1 post contrast; C, coronal T2; and D, sagittal T1 post contrast showing a symmetrical pituitary gland enlargement with convex superior margin (dotted arrow in A), and marked T2 hypointensity (dotted arrow in C), which was initially considered to be a pituitary adenoma because of a misinterpreted central nodule (white arrow in B and C).
in_text_mentions: Due to the diagnosis of MEN1, screening for pituitary tumor was performed at age 38. Mild hyperprolactinemia (26 µg/L; reference range, 5-23 µg/L), along with biochemical evidence of acromegaly (elevated insulin-growth factor 1 [IGF-I] 701 ng/mL [SI: 91.6 nmol/L] [reference range, 63-223 ng/mL (SI: 8.2-29.2 mL)]), and random GH concentration of 7.4 ng/mL. No physical signs of acromegaly were observed on examination. Sellar magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed a central sellar nodule of 9 × 8 × 6 mm, initially considered to be a pituitary adenoma (Fig. 2).

ratively, she developed severe hypoglycemia (capillary glucose 40-50 mg/dL, SI: 2.2-2.8 mmol/L) requiring hospitalization. Histopathological examination of the pituitary tissue revealed somatotroph hyperplasia (Fig. 3). Sellar MRI was reviewed and showed a symmetrical pituitary gland enlargement with convex superior margin, and T2 hypointensity, suggestive of pituitary hyperplasia (see Fig. 2). Postoperative GH and IGF-I concentrations decreased, but did not normalize (GH 3.7 ng/mL; IGF-I 419 ng/mL [SI: 54.8 nmol/L]). Plasma GHRH measurement was not available in the patient's country (Brazil).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A is a venous-phase CT image from a MEN1 case report showing the patient's pancreatic head mass, consistent with a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor. B: Panel B is an arterial-phase CT image from the same MEN1 case report showing the patient's pancreatic head mass, consistent with a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor. C: Panel C is a CT image from a MEN1 case report showing a right adrenal low-density nodule that was clinically interpreted as an adrenal adenoma. This is an associated finding in MEN1, but the specific adrenal adenoma finding is not represented in the provided vocabulary, so it is captured as a proposed finding.

findings.label: Pituitary macroadenoma
findings.evidence: Caption: '(NMR) pituitary macroadenoma and left superior parietal extra-axial lesion compatible with meningioma.' In-text: 'A nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) revealed a pituitary macroadenoma of 20 × 13 × 15 mm which spread to the right cavernous sinus, with displacement of the optic chiasm.'

panels.rationale: Single sagittal contrast brain MRI from the reported MEN1 case shows a sellar/suprasellar pituitary macroadenoma, with in-text support for cavernous sinus spread and optic chiasm displacement, plus an extra-axial parietal lesion compatible with meningioma. The disease-focused article title and caption support attribution of the pituitary macroadenoma to MEN1. The parietal meningioma is captioned but has no allowed vocabulary key, so it is recorded as a proposed finding. No age, ethnicity, skin surface, or annotations are assessable.

panels.figure_caption: (NMR) pituitary macroadenoma and left superior parietal extra-axial lesion compatible with meningioma.
in_text_mentions: The endocrine study confirmed the clinical suspicion of primary hyperparathyroidism and GH hypersecretion. The parathyroid SPECT/CT was compatible with right parathyroid adenoma. A nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) revealed a pituitary macroadenoma of 20 × 13 × 15 mm which spread to the right cavernous sinus, with displacement of the optic chiasm, and a left superior extra-axial parietal lesion of 20 × 20 × 12 mm which suggested a meningioma (Figure 1).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: H&E of the ovarian surgical specimen showing a trabecular neuroendocrine pattern; the article is a MEN1 case report and the in-text diagnoses an atypical carcinoid subtype, so the panel shows a MEN1-associated neuroendocrine tumor manifestation. [raw subtype: atypical carcinoid] B: High-power H&E of the same ovarian tumor showing >2 mitoses per 10 HPF with atypical nuclei, supporting the atypical carcinoid diagnosis in this MEN1 case; mitotic rate is not in the allowed vocabulary so it is proposed. [raw subtype: atypical carcinoid] C: H&E of the ovarian carcinoid showing foci of necrosis, a feature of the atypical carcinoid in this MEN1 case report; necrosis is not in the allowed vocabulary so it is proposed. [raw subtype: atypical carcinoid] D: Immunohistochemistry of the right ovarian tumor showing diffuse synaptophysin positivity, confirming neuroendocrine differentiation of the MEN1-associated atypical carcinoid; marker...

panels.figure_caption: Histological examination of the surgical specimen of the ovary showed that the main part of the tumor had a trabecular pattern, but an insular pattern was also observed in some sections of the tumor, original magnification, × 200 (a), more than 2 mitosis per 10 high-power field, original magnification, × 400 (b) and foci of necrosis, original magnification, × 400 (c). Immunohistochemistry analysis of a tumor sample from the right ovary demonstrating positive detection of synaptophysin, original magnification, × 200 (d), CgA, × 200 (e), and staining index for Ki-67 was between 10 and 15%, × 200 (f)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Contrast-enhanced CT showing a heterogeneous enhancing mass in the rib (white arrow). The caption describes enhancement in the ribs and the in-text states Fig. 2 shows 'metastases to the bones and liver' in a patient with MEN1 and multivisceral neuroendocrine tumor spread, supporting attribution to MEN1. B: Contrast-enhanced CT showing a heterogeneous enhancing lesion in the anterior mediastinum (white arrow). The caption groups it with the other hypervascular masses and the in-text describes 'multivisceral spread of the neuroendocrine tumors' in this MEN1 case; PET-CT also notes thymic hypermetabolism, supporting a thymic neuroendocrine lesion. C: Contrast-enhanced CT showing a hypervascular pancreatic mass (white arrow). Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor is a classic manifestation of MEN1, and the in-text confirms multivisceral neuroendocrine tumor spread in this MEN1 case. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: MIP 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT of a 66-year-old MEN1 patient (DK-59) showing a somatostatin-receptor-avid liver lesion (red arrow), consistent with metastatic neuroendocrine tumor in the setting of metastatic Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. B: Axial fused 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT showing the liver metastasis with DOTATATE uptake (white arrow, SUVmax 14.0) in a MEN1 patient with metastatic Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. C: MIP 18F-FDOPA PET/CT showing intense uptake of the liver metastasis (red arrow) in the same MEN1 patient, confirming metastatic neuroendocrine tumor. D: Axial fused 18F-FDOPA PET/CT showing intense tracer uptake in the liver metastasis (white arrow, SUVmax 45.0) in a MEN1 patient. E: Axial contrast CT showing the 3.0 cm liver metastasis (black arrow) corresponding to the PET findings in a MEN1 patient with metastatic Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. F: Axial MRI showing the corresponding 3.0 cm liver metastasis (black arrow) in the...

panels.figure_caption: A 66-year-old man with MEN1 (DK-59) complicated by metastatic Zollinger–Ellison syndrome and gastric carcinoids. (A, B) 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT demonstrates limited/partial lesion uptake in the liver on maximum intensity projection (red arrow) and axial view (white arrow); SUV maximum 14.0. (C, D) 18F-FDOPA PET/CT demonstrates increased uptake of the liver metastases on maximum intensity projection (red arrow) and axial view (white arrow); SUV maximum 45.0. (E, F) CT and MRI show corresponding liver metastases measuring 3.0 cm (black arrow).
in_text_mentions: 1% of the liver lesions (2/28; 95% CI: 0%–19.1%) with a SUVmax of 45 and 58, respectively. Interestingly, 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT and 18F-FDOPA PET/CT co-localized a liver metastasis with subtle 68Ga-DOTATATE uptake yet intense 18F-FDOPA PET/CT uptake in patient DK-59 (Figure 2). This patient had a urinary 5-HIAA that was three times the upper limit of normal, suggesting the functionality of this lesion. Liver lesions highly suspicious for metastasis were noted on CT/MRI in DK-526 with a known history of insulinoma. These lesions were not seen on 18F-FDOPA PET/CT and 68Ga-DOTATATE (Figures 3A–D).

[raw subtype: pancreatic_net] B: Real patient abdominal T1-weighted coronal MRI with a yellow arrow marking the same pancreatic lesion. in_text_mentions: rmal limits (insulin: 6.0 µU/mL reference: 1-35 µU/mL, C-peptide: 0.903 nmol/L, reference: 0.34-2.33 nmol/L), proinsulin was elevated (63 pmol/L, reference: 3.6-22 pmol/L), which was suggestive of a diagnosis of insulinoma. The patient was started on diazoxide therapy, while a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the abdomen was performed to identify potential NETs and possible metastases. The MRI of his abdomen revealed multiple pancreatic masses, the largest measuring 2.8 x 1.3 cm, with diffusion restriction and variable enhancement within the pancreas, consistent with insulinomas (Figure 1).

Real patient image, clearly captioned, attributed to MEN1 by both the article title and the MEN1-specific multigard pattern. [raw subtype: multigland parathyroid hyperplasia] B: Delayed-phase SESTAMIBI scan of the same MEN1 patient showing persistent tracer uptake in the three parathyroid glands, confirming parathyroid adenomas. Multigard parathyroid disease is the classic presenting manifestation of MEN1; the article title and caption attribute this to MEN1. Real patient radiology image, clear quality, no third-party copyright issue.

in_text_mentions: Upon admission in January 2025, the patient presented with altered mental status, dehydration, and hypoglycemia. The recurrence of hypoglycemic episodes was confirmed by laboratory studies and imaging, which identified a well-defined 3 cm mass in the pancreatic head on triphasic computed tomography (Figs 1–3). Given the diagnosis of recurrent malignant insulinoma and the possibility of resection, a surgical approach was chosen.

panels.rationale: Single axial abdominal MRI from a human patient whose workup was performed for MEN1 (in-text: 'an extensive workup for evaluation of MEN was done... on abdominal MRI (Figure 1)') in an article titled 'Zollinger Ellison Syndrome in a Patient with Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 1'. The image shows a pancreatic cystic lesion indicated by arrows, corresponding to a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor manifestation of MEN1, plus diffuse gastric wall thickening (4.52 cm) consistent with the described ZES presentation. Prior caption triage kept this as real human radiology. No third-party copyright indicated. Not a diagram, control, or other-disease panel. [raw subtype: zollinger_ellison_syndrome]

panels.figure_caption: MRI abdomen showing diffuse gastric wall thickening (4.52 cm) with a small pancreatic cystic lesion (arrows).
in_text_mentions: pg/mL). She did not have any history of prior gastric surgeries, gastroparesis, or renal disease, to possibly explain her elevated gastrin level. An infectious workup for her diarrhea, including Clostridium difficile toxin and a stool PCR panel for common enteric pathogens, was negative. Subsequently, an extensive workup for evaluation of MEN was done, which revealed a unilateral parathyroid adenoma on neck imaging and diffuse stomach wall thickening along with pancreatic cystic lesions in body (1.2 cm) and tail (0.7 cm) on abdominal MRI (Figure 1). Testing for pituitary disease was negative.

panels.figure_caption: Ga-68-DOTANOC scan images of the patient Maximum intensity projection (MIP) image (A) and axial fused positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) images (B and C) show two somatostatin receptor expressing lesions in the pancreatic head (1.6 cm x 1.5 cm) (B) and tail region (3.2 cm x 2.2 cm) (C), respectively.
in_text_mentions: Patient also underwent Ga-68-DOTANOC positron emission tomography (PET)/computed tomography (CT) that revealed somatostatin receptor (SSTR) expressing lesions in the head of the pancreas (1.6 cm x 1.5 cm) and tail of the pancreas (3.2 cm x 2.2 cm) (Figures 4A-4C). She also underwent endoscopic ultrasonography (EUS) that revealed multiple hypoechoic round lesions in the pancreas (max: 3.5 cm x 2.1 cm x 0.8 cm) with vascularity in the lesions, two lesions of diameter 2.1 cm and 1.1 cm in the body of pancreas, and four small lesions in the tail of pancreas (~8 mm each).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: H&E of the patient's pancreatic insulinoma from an MEN1 case (article title: MEN1 presenting with concurrent insulinoma and prolactinoma in early-adolescence); shows neuroendocrine tumor histology, a direct manifestation of MEN1. B: Congo red histochemical stain of the same patient's insulinoma showing amyloid deposition, a recognized feature of insulinomas in MEN1; real human-patient tissue, disease attribution supported by caption and MEN1 article title. C: Synaptophysin immunohistochemistry of the patient's pancreatic insulinoma confirming neuroendocrine differentiation; in-text mention confirms synaptophysin positivity on aspirate, consistent with MEN1-associated insulinoma. D: Ki67 immunohistochemistry of the same patient's insulinoma showing a 1–2% proliferation index, confirming low-grade MEN1-associated insulinoma; in-text mention corroborates 2–3% Ki-67 on aspirate.

panels.body_site: whole body (coronal FDG PET-CT maximum-intensity projection)
panels.rationale: Single whole-body coronal FDG PET-CT image (lesion markers 1-6, not separate panels) from an MEN1 case report. It shows multiglandular metabolically active lesions that are core MEN1 manifestations: an upper-abdominal/peripancreatic mass corresponding to the pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor confirmed on CT, a left adrenal lesion (adenoma on CT), and a prevascular/anterior mediastinal lesion consistent with paraganglioma. Real human-patient nuclear medicine image with clear numbered annotations; breast, thyroid and endometrial foci are also captioned but the pancreatic NET/adrenal/paraganglioma pattern establishes MEN1 attribution.
panels.attribution_text: JEONG et al. Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 associated with breast cancer: A case report and review of the literature.. Oncology letters 2014. doi:10.3892/ol.2014.2144. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Findings of positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT). PET-CT showed (1) a metabolically mildly active right breast lesion compatible with the proven right breast cancer, which was proven by an ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy (2) a metabolically mildly active left thyroid lesion, which was suspicious for thyroid cancer, (3) a metabolically active prevascular (ascending paraaortic) nodal lesion, (4) metabolically active upper abdominal nodal lesions (left gastric lymph node and adjacent to hepatic and splenic artery), which were suspicious for metastatic nodal lesions or a primary pancreas tail mass (4), (5) suspicious left adrenal metastasis and (6) mild endometrial uptake, which was suspicious for myoma or endometrial malignancy.
in_text_mentions: r. PET-CT showed metabolically active lesions in the right breast, the anterior mediastinum, the peripancreatic area of the upper abdomen and the left adrenal gland, which corresponded to the lesions observed on the CT scan (Fig. 2). In addition, the left thyroid gland and the endometrium of the uterus showed mild FDG uptake on the PET-CT, and a suspicious metastatic nodule of the lung was observed on the CT scan. The findings of an additional abdominopelvic CT scan indicated a neuroendocrine tumor of the pancreas, paraganglioma, a left adrenal adenoma, gallstones and uterine subserosal myoma.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Gross resected distal splenopancreatectomy specimen showing inferior-border pancreatic neoplasia in article about functioning glucagonoma with primary hyperparathyroidism evaluated as MEN1. Caption describes exophytic well-circumscribed pancreatic neoplasia corresponding to 3x2x2 cm neuroendocrine tumor, supporting MEN1 enteropancreatic NET. B: Cut surface view of same resected pancreatic neoplasia. Caption specifies whitish-yellow cut surface with focal hemorrhage, consistent with pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor in MEN1-workup case of functioning glucagonoma with hyperparathyroidism.

in_text_mentions: was discharged 11 days after the operation in good condition. The resected specimen contained a tumor measuring 3×2×2 cm in diameter, corresponding to the lesion identified by imaging studies (Figure 5). On histopathological examination the tumor appeared encapsulated, well vascularized, and composed of polygonal cells with trabecular or ribbon-like proliferation. Four mitoses per 10 HPF (High Power Field) were observed. No lymphatic, blood vessel or perineural invasions were found. Immunohistochemistry showed a 5% Ki-67 index and intense diffuse staining for non-specific neuroendocrine marker

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Real patient gastric biopsy (H&E, green arrows) from the Zollinger-Ellison workup of a patient whose article title frames MEN1 with a classic ZES presentation. Hypertrophic gastric mucosa is the expected trophic response to marked hypergastrinemia/acid hypersecretion of ZES, a recognized MEN1 manifestation; intestinal metaplasia is nonspecific. No vocabulary key covers gastric findings, so they are listed as proposed. Included with moderate confidence because gastritis/metaplasia alone are not specific to MEN1. b: Pancreatic cyst FNA cytology (circled area) showing neuroendocrine cells / well-differentiated NET, i.e. a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor, a direct and classic manifestation of MEN1; matched by the enteropancreatic NET histology key. Disease attribution and finding are both explicit, so high confidence.

in_text_mentions: flux esophagitis, diffusely hypertrophic gastric rugae and multiple postbulbar ulcers in the duodenum (Figures 2(a), 2(b), and 2(c)). Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) subsequently revealed diffuse thickening of the gastric rugae, predominantly of echo-layers I-III (Figure 3(a)). In addition, the patient was found to have a cystic lesion in the pancreatic neck with thick hypoechoic walls (Figure 3(b)). Random biopsies of the gastric antrum and body revealed patchy chronic gastritis with intestinal metaplasia (Figure 4(a)) while FNA from pancreatic cyst revealed well differentiated NET (Figure 4(b)).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Sagittal contrast-enhanced pituitary MRI of the MEN1 index patient showing a small hypointense nodular lesion in the right lobe of the pituitary gland (red arrow), described as a pituitary microadenoma. The article title and in-text confirm MEN1 (whole-exome sequencing for clinical suspicion of MEN1), and pituitary adenomas are a cardinal manifestation of MEN1, so disease attribution is strong. The lesion is <1 cm, i.e., a microadenoma, which is a less common imaging form than the macroadenoma vocabulary term; hence tagged as variant and the microadenoma term proposed. [raw subtype: pituitary microadenoma] B: Coronal contrast-enhanced pituitary MRI of the same MEN1 patient, displaying the hypointense nodular lesion in the right lobe of the pituitary gland (red arrow), consistent with a pituitary microadenoma. Same lesion and disease attribution as the sagittal view; pituitary adenomas are a hallmark of MEN1, confirmed here by the article...

panels.rationale: Single axial contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen centered on the pancreas, with a small circle annotation marking a slightly hypodense 1.1 × 0.4 cm pancreatic lesion circumscribed by calcification. The image comes from an MEN1 case report with suspected Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, and the captioned pancreatic lesion corresponds to a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor manifestation of MEN1, so disease attribution is supported by both the disease-focused title and the panel-specific caption. The hypodense, peripherally calcified appearance is a less common CT presentation of the typically hypervascular pancreatic NET, hence variant. No ethnicity or age is stated; no skin is assessable on CT. [raw subtype: pancreatic_net]

panels.rationale: Axial non-contrast CT of the abdomen showing coarse calcification in the pancreatic head (indicated by the white arrow) in a patient with MEN1 and suspected Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. The article title is disease-focused (MEN1), and the in-text specifically describes this pancreatic head calcification. In the context of MEN1, a calcified lesion in the pancreatic head is suspicious for a calcified pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (gastrinoma), which is a recognized MEN1 manifestation. The calcification itself is not in the allowed vocabulary, so it is also listed as a proposed finding. Confidence is moderate because pancreatic calcification is nonspecific, but the MEN1 context, the pancreatic head location, and the suspected ZES support attribution to a pancreatic NET rather than an unrelated finding.

Clinical photo: large elastic mass in right cervical region (green circle); corresponding neck ultrasonography shows an isoechoic mass. Article title identifies the mass as a giant cervical lipoma accompanying MEN1.
Neck ultrasonography: two parathyroid tumors with maximal diameters 38 mm (arrows) and 14 mm (arrow heads); in-text: intact-parathyroid hormone (PTH) level was high (273 pg/mL).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Contrast-enhanced brain MRI from a human MEN1 patient showing a ~50 mm sellar/suprasellar mass with cavernous sinus invasion and optic nerve compression, matching the vocabulary finding of pituitary macroadenoma, one of the classic MEN1 triad manifestations. B: Clinical photograph with corresponding neck ultrasound from a human MEN1 patient showing a large elastic cervical mass that the disease-focused article title identifies as a giant cervical lipoma; subcutaneous lipomas are a recognized MEN1 cutaneous manifestation, and a giant cervical lipoma is a less common (variant) presentation. C: Neck ultrasound from a human MEN1 patient showing two enlarged parathyroid glands with elevated intact PTH, consistent with multigland parathyroid hyperplasia, the classic and most common MEN1 manifestation.

plate_findings.evidence: The tumor cells had uniform rounded nuclei and pale acidophilic cytoplasm; no mitotic cells were found

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: H&E-stained pancreatic biopsy showing classic well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor histology in a patient with MEN1. B: Synaptophysin immunohistochemistry of pancreatic tumor, supporting neuroendocrine differentiation in a MEN1-associated pancreatic NET. C: Chromogranin A immunohistochemistry of pancreatic tumor, supporting neuroendocrine differentiation in a MEN1-associated pancreatic NET. D: Anti-gastrin immunohistochemistry of pancreatic NET; negative staining supports a non-functional pancreatic NET, but the panel itself shows negative immunostaining rather than a positive manifestation.
panels.attribution_text: Hirakawa et al. Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumor Leading to a Diagnosis of Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 1.. DEN open 2026. doi:10.1002/deo2.70160. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Microscopic observations for the pancreatic tumor. A pancreatic biopsy was performed, and the sample was analyzed by hematoxylin‐eosin staining (A) and immunohistochemical detection using (B) anti‐synaptophysin, (C) anti‐chromogranin A, and (D) anti‐gastrin. The tumor cells had uniform rounded nuclei and pale acidophilic cytoplasm. Scale bar, 50 µm. No mitotic cells were found. The tumor showed synaptophysin and chromogranin positivity, with a Ki‐67 labeling index of less than 1%. The tumor did not express gastrin.
in_text_mentions: harmonic EUS with a sonographic contrast agent (Sonazoid; Daiichi‐Sankyo, Tokyo, Japan) showed enhancement of the mass in the pancreatic body from an early stage. EUS‐guided fine‐needle biopsy (FNB) with a 22‐gauge needle (Acquire; Boston Scientific, Marlborough, MA, USA) was performed on the mass in the pancreatic body via the stomach. Pathology showed tumor cells with uniform rounded nuclei and pale acidophilic cytoplasm. The diagnosis was pancreatic NET (P‐NET) (G1) (Figure 3). Immunostaining showed negativity for gastrin, insulin, and glucagon, leading to a diagnosis of non‐functional NET.
